evals.prompt: Set up guardrails for a support agent that can query our customer database. It sees names, emails, and phone numbers.
evals.expected_output: A six-layer pipeline with SELECT-only SQL enforcement and PII scrubbing on output, wired into the request path, with tests per layer.
expectations: The generated pipeline covers input schema validation, content filtering, semantic analysis, tool guardrails, and output guardrails
SQL validation rejects INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE, DROP, ALTER, and TRUNCATE
Output scrubbing covers email and phone number patterns
An integration snippet shows the pipeline wired into the request handler
Tests are generated with both blocking and passing cases for each layer

evals.prompt: People keep jailbreaking our chatbot. Someone got it to print its system prompt yesterday.
evals.expected_output: Injection detection plus a semantic extraction check and a system-prompt-leak check on output, with a test corpus.
expectations: Regex detection for instruction-override phrasing such as ignore previous instructions is included
A semantic check for system prompt extraction attempts is included
An output check for system prompt fragments leaking into the response is included
The response recommends wrapping external content in untrusted markers
Negative test cases are included so benign queries are not blocked

evals.prompt: Our agent runs Python that users supply. What guardrails do I need?
evals.expected_output: A sandbox specification with network disabled, read-only filesystem, resource limits, and a non-root user, plus tests proving each restriction holds.
expectations: The sandbox configuration sets network access to none
The sandbox runs as a non-root user
Memory, CPU, or wall-clock resource limits are specified
The filesystem is read-only or restricted to a scratch directory
A test is included that asserts network access fails from inside the sandbox
